jobs.title: The Florence paper
jobs.prompt: a four-panel newspaper comic strip, four equal panels in a single horizontal row with thin black gutters (4 panels). Style: comic strip panel, black brush-pen ink line with muddy early-2000s digital flat colors, rubbery kinetic linework, mid-2000s webcomic look, limited palette, slightly misregistered fills. Cast, the same faces, hair and builds in every panel, ages exactly as given: WOOD — aged 28, thin man, hunched, unshaven, tired bloodshot eyes, ink on his right knuckle; BARNABY (the dog) — a low-slung terrier and hound mix, long body, short legs, folded velvet ears, wiry white-and-tan coat, gray on the muzzle from 2004, cloudy eyes from 2009, carried from 2010. WOOD usually wears black hoodie open over a faded band tee; the brown chore coat outdoors; dark jeans. Clothes, hair-dos and anything held come from this strip's description, never from the reference sheet; hands are empty unless a panel names what they hold. Title of the strip: DRIFT WOOD. The strip: Saturday. Florence's reply: the gull restored, and, by mistake or not, printed twice as big. Wood pins that page over the parody on the corkboard, where the Feb 25 page already is. Two pages over one parody. Panel 1: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, a thin man looking at a newspaper strip where the tiny signature gull has been printed enormous, a small dog (in this panel: WOOD, BARNABY (the dog)). Panel 2: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, close-up of a newspaper comic where a signature gull mark is printed larger than the dog in the strip. Panel 3: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, a thin man holding a newspaper and speaking to a small dog, dry (in this panel: WOOD, BARNABY (the dog)). Panel 4: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, a thin man pinning a second newspaper page over a first on a corkboard, both covering a printout beneath, a large gull mark facing out, no words (in this panel: WOOD). No text, no lettering, no speech balloons, no signature; leave clean space in each panel where balloons would go. Reference @barnaby is the model sheet for BARNABY (the dog): match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @wood_26 is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @loc_garage shows the setting; keep its architecture and props. Match the attached references: @barnaby for the character Barnaby; @wood_26 for the character Wood at 24-31; @loc_garage for the setting.
